title: About A/B testing for Meta Ads

facts.fact: Meta's A/B testing compares two versions of an ad strategy by changing variables such as ad images, ad text, audience or placement, with each version shown to a segment of the audience so nobody sees both.
facts.quote: A/B testing enables you to compare two versions of an ad strategy by changing variables such as ad images, ad text, audience or placement. Each version is shown to a segment of your audience, ensuring nobody sees both

facts.fact: When creating a Meta A/B test by duplicating an existing campaign, ad set or ad, the ad budget is also duplicated.
facts.quote: If you choose to duplicate an existing campaign, your ad budget is also duplicated.

facts.fact: Meta advises using the same budget for both versions in an A/B test to ensure a fair comparison.
facts.quote: Use the same budget for both versions in a test to ensure a fair comparison.

facts.fact: Meta's A/B testing measures each strategy's performance on a cost per result basis or a cost per conversion lift basis.
facts.quote: A/B testing can then measure the performance of each strategy on a cost per result basis or cost per conversion lift basis.

facts.fact: Meta does not recommend informal A/B testing by manually turning ad sets or campaigns on and off, because it can lead to inefficient ad delivery and unreliable results.
facts.quote: We do not recommend testing informally, such as by turning ad sets or campaigns on and off manually. Informal testing can lead to inefficient ad delivery and unreliable test results.

facts.fact: Meta states that A/B testing helps ensure audiences are evenly split and statistically comparable, whereas informal testing can lead to overlapping audiences.
facts.quote: A/B testing helps ensure your audiences will be evenly split and statistically comparable, while informal testing can lead to overlapping audiences.
